notes: Summary: Fulcrum CodeRecall — internal engineering and developer-facing code search platform. Building RAG for code intelligence across 120M files (monorepos + mirrors).
Primary pain: scale of embeddings (>120M shards), frequent re-index (daily deltas), strict cost per query targets for 100k qps bursts.
Targets: p95 retrieval + rerank <= 150ms, tail sensitivity for dev flow; cost <= $0.002/query; support reranking top-50 candidates with cross-encoder scoring.
Model preference: open LLMs for rerank (Llama2/Meta, Mistral variants), quantized encoder/bi-encoder for embeddings; fallback to smaller models when under heavy load.
Security: IdP SSO (SAML), enterprise audit trails, KMS for envelope keys, retention controls for embeddings (90d retention), EU data residency for EU repos.
POC done: 2-week POC used 8xA100 equivalent on Dedicated; built embedding pipeline with incremental re-indexing; initial index size ~1.2 PB (raw); embedding store ~1.6 TB.
POC results: recall within top-50 good, but rerank CPU cost high — cross-encoder at scale spikes GPU utilization; batching and quantization candidates discussed. See latency-report.
Quote from CTO (call 2026-02-18): 'We can't accept >200ms for code suggestions — developer flow is unforgiving.'
Current approaches evaluated: RedisVectors for hot prefix cache, hybrid HNSW + product-quantization, sharding by repo/team, selective rerank to top-20 instead of 50 to save cost.
Open questions: best practice for frequent re-indexing w/ minimal downtime; live-update of ANN indices; KV cache invalidation strategy.
Sales touchpoints: Demo 2026-01-28 (Samira + Diego), Architecture deep-dive 2026-02-25, Security review 2026-03-05 with security team (legal invited).
Next steps (from AE): run quantization A/B (8-bit vs 4-bit) on cross-encoder, cost modeling for monthly reindex operations, formal SAML metadata exchange.
Blockers repeated in notes: IdP metadata, legal on EU residency clause, POC latency > target when scaling.
